senses.gloss: पितामह पिता-मह. See p. 574, col. 1.

पितु पितु, उस्, m., Ved. (fr. rt. प्यै),
juice, drink; nourishment; (Sāy.) = पालकम् अन्-
नम्, nourishing food.
—पितु-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved.
bestowing or providing food.
—पितु-भाज्, क्, क्, क्,
Ved. enjoying or partaking of food; (Sāy.) = अन्-
नार्थिन्, seeking or earning food.
—पितु-भृत्, त्,
त्, त्, Ved. bringing food.
—पितु-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्,
Ved. accompanied by food, abounding in food, nou-
rishing.
—पितु-षणि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. bestowing or
granting food.
—पितु-स्तोम, अस्, m. ‘praise of
food,’ N. of the hymn Ṛg-veda I. 187.

पीतु पीतु, उस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 1. पा,
but perhaps fr. rt. पिव्), the sun; fire; the chief
elephant of a herd.
—पीतु-दारु, उस्, m. = देव-
दारु, q. v.; (according to others) = खदिर, a tree
related to the Uḍumbara; (अम्), n. the resin of this
tree; [cf. पूतु-दारु; Gr. πί-τυ-ς, πίσσα for πι-
κ-ια; Lat. pī-nu-s, pix; Lith. pī1ki-s, ‘pitch.’]

पितूय, Nom. P. पितूयति, -यितुम्, Ved. to long
for food, desire food.

पितृ पितृ, ता, m. (fr. rt. 3. पा), a father;
(in the Veda पितृ is an epithet of Bṛhas-pati,
Varuṇa, Prajā-pati, and especially of heaven or the
[]
sky; अन्तरा पितरम् मातरञ्-च, between heaven
and earth; according to Sāy. पितृ = पालक, a
protector); (तरौ), m. du. father and mother,
parents, (in the Veda an epithet of the Araṇis or
two pieces of wood regarded as the parents of Fire,
and of heaven and earth regarded as the parents of
all beings); (तरस्), m. pl. fathers, forefathers,
ancestors; a father and his brothers, father and
uncles, paternal ancestors; the spirits of departed an-
cestors, the Manes or spirits of the dead (they are of
two kinds, viz. either the spirits of the father, grand-
fathers, and great-grandfathers of an individual or the
progenitors of mankind generally, to both classes of
whom Śrāddhas or obsequial worship is paid and
oblations of food called Piṇḍas presented; they in-
habit a peculiar region, which, according to some, is
the Bhuvas or region of the air, according to others,
the orbit of the moon, and are considered as the
regents of the Nakṣatras Maghā and Mūla); [cf.
Zend pita, base pa-tar: Gr. πα-τήρ, πάτρω-ς:
Lat. pa-ter, Jup-piter: Goth. fa-dar: Old
Germ. fa-tar, fa-ter, ‘father;’ fataro, ‘uncle:’
Angl. Sax. faeder, ‘father;’ fadhu, ‘aunt,
father's sister:’ Hib. athair, ‘father,’ for pathair.],
—पितरि-शूर, अस्, m. ‘a hero against his father,’
a cowardly boaster.
—पिता-पुत्र, औ, m. du. father
and son.
—पितापुत्र-विरोध, अस्, m. a contest
between father and son.
—पितापुत्र-समागम,
अस्, m., N. of a Buddhist Sūtra.
—पितापुत्रीय, अस्,
आ, अम्, relating to father and son; containing the
words पितृ and पुत्र; (with सम्प्रदान) the
transmission (of bodily capacities and powers) from
father to son.
—पिता-मह, अस्, m. a paternal
grandfather; a N. of Brahmā the great father of all;
N. of the author of a Dharma-śāstra; of the author
of an astronomical work; (आस्), m. pl. the ancestors,
Manes; (ई), f. a paternal grandmother.
—पितामह-
सरस्, अस्, n. or पितामहस्य सरस्, N. of a place
of pilgrimage.
—पिता-सुमति-संवाद, अस्, m., N.
of a part of the Brahma-vaivarta-Purāṇa.
—पितुः-
पुत्र, अस्, m. a father's son.
—पितुः-ष्वसृ or
पितुः-स्वसृ, सा, f. a father's sister.
—पितृ-कर्मन्,
अ, or पितृ-कार्य, अम्, n. obsequial rites, sacrifice
offered to deceased ancestors.
—पितृ-कल्प, अस्, m.
(perhaps) legends relating to ancestors; N. of a long
period of time, Brahmā's day of new moon.
—पितृ-
कानन, अम्, n. ‘grove of ancestors,’ a cemetery.
—पितृ-कुल्या, f. ‘rivulet of the Pitṛs,’ N. of a
river rising in the Malaya mountains.
—पितृ-कृत,
अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. committed against parents or an-
cestors (as sin).
—पितृ-कृत्य, अम्, n. or पितृ-
क्रिया, f. obsequial rites, oblations offered to the
spirits of deceased ancestors.
—पितृ-गण, अस्, m.
the whole body of ancestors collectively, a group or
class of Manes or deceased progenitors who were
sons of the Ṛṣis or Prajā-patis, (the principal classes,
according to Manu III. 194-199, are the Soma-sads,
descended from Vi-rāj, the Agni-ṣvāttas from Marīci,
Barhi-shads from Atri, Soma-pās from Bhṛgu, Haviṣ-
mats from Aṅgiras, Ājya-pas from Pulastya, and
Su-kālins from Vasiṣṭha; there are also the Agni-
dagdhas and An-agnidagdhas, Kāvyas and Saumyas.)
—पितृ-गणा, f. an epithet of Durgā.
—पितृ-
गाथा, आस्, f. pl. ‘songs of the ancestors,’ an epithet
of particular songs.
—पितृ-गामिन्, ई, इनी, इ, be-
longing or pertaining to a father.
—पितृ-गृणा, f.
probably a wrong reading for पितृ-गणा, q. v.
—पितृ-गृह, अम्, n. a father's house, paternal
mansion; ‘house of ancestors,’ a burial ground, ceme-
tery.
—पितृ-ग्रह, अस्, m. ‘the genius of the
Manes,’ N. of a demon causing disease.
—पितृ-
घातक, अस्, or पितृ-घातिन्, ई, m. ‘slaying a
father,’ a parricide.
—पितृ-चेट, अस्, m., N. of a
man.
—पितृ-तम, अस्, m., Ved., in पितृतमः
पित्रीणां, best of the ancestors (Sāy. = पाल-
कानाम् मध्ये अतिशयेन पालकः, a defender in
the highest degree among defenders).
—पितृ-तर्-
पण, अम्, n. ‘refreshing the Manes,’ gifts in
honour of deceased progenitors, distributed at the
Śrāddhas or funeral ceremonies; an oblation to the
Manes; the act of throwing water out of the right
[]
hand at seasons of ablution as an offering to the
Manes or deceased ancestors in general; the part of
the hand between the thumb and fore-finger sacred
to the Manes; sesamum (= तिल).
—पितृ-तस्, ind.,
Ved. from the father, on the father's side.
—पितृ-
तिथि, इस्, f. day of new moon, a day sacred to the
Manes of either deceased parent, the day appointed
for obsequial rites to deceased ancestors.
—पितृ-
तीर्थ, अम्, n. ‘the place of pilgrimage for proge-
nitors,’ epithet of the city called Gayā (where the
performance of funeral sacrifices is peculiarly meri-
torious and efficacious); the part of the hand be-
tween the fore-finger and thumb sacred to the
Manes.
—पितृतीर्थ-माहात्म्य, अम्, n., N. of a
chapter of the Śiva-Purāṇa.
—पितृ-त्व, अम्, n.
fatherhood, paternity; the state or condition of a
Pitṛ or deified progenitor.
—पितृ-दत्त, अस्, आ,
अम्, given by a father (a term applied to a woman's
peculiar property); (अस्), m., N. of a man.
—पितृ-
दयिता, f., N. of a work.
—पितृ-दान or पितृ-
दानक, अम्, n. a gift in honour of deceased an-
cestors, an offering to the Manes.
—पितृ-दाय,
अस्, m. property inherited from a father, patrimony.
—पितृ-देव, आस्, m. pl. the Manes and the gods;
the divine Manes; (अस्, आ, अम्), worshipping a
father; relating to the worship of the Manes or
deceased ancestors.
—पितृ-देवत or पितृ-देवत्य,
अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having the Manes for deities,
sacred to the Manes.
—पितृ-दैवत, अस्, ई, अम्,
relating to the worship of the Manes; governed or
presided over by the Manes; (अम्), n. epithet of the
tenth lunar asterism or Maghā.
—पितृ-दैवत्य,
अस्, आ, अम्, relating to the worship of the Manes;
(अम्), n., N. of a sacrifice offered to the Manes on
the day called Aṣṭakā.
—पितृ-द्रव्य, अम्, n.
‘father's substance,’ patrimony.
—पितृ-नामन्, आ,
म्नी, अ, called after the father's name; [cf. मातृ-
नामन्.]
—पितृ-पक्ष, अस्, m. paternal side,
paternal relationship; the half month of the Manes,
N. of the dark half in the Gauṇa Āśvina, so termed
as peculiarly appointed for the celebration of obse-
quial rites to the Pitṛs or Manes; a father's relations,
relatives by the father's side; (अस्, आ, अम्), being on
the father's side.
—पितृ-पति, इस्, m. ‘lord of the
Manes,’ an epithet of Yama, regent of the dead;
(अयस्), m. pl. the Manes and the lords of creatures
(Prajā-patis).
—पितृ-पद, अम्, n. the world or
state of the Manes.
—पितृ-पात्र, अम्, n. a cup or
other vessel used at obsequial rites.
—पितृ-पितृ, ता,
m. a father's father, paternal grandfather.
—पितृ-
पीत, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. drunk by ancestors or deceased
progenitors.
—पितृ-पूजन, अम्, n. worship of the
Manes.
—पितृ-पैतामह, अस्, ई, अम्, inherited or
derived from father and grandfather; (आस्), m. pl.
fathers and grandfathers, ancestors.
—पितृपैता-
महिक, अस्, ई, अम्, inherited or derived from father
and grandfather.
—पितृ-प्रसू, ऊस्, f. a father's
mother; ‘mother of the Manes,’ twilight (the time
when the Manes of departed ancestors are abroad).
—पितृ-प्राप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, received from a father;
inherited patrimonially.
—पितृ-प्रिय, अस्, m. ‘dear
to the Pitṛs,’ a species of plant (= भृङ्ग-राज).
—पितृ-बन्धु, उस्, m. a kinsman by the father's
side, as the son of the paternal grandfather's sister,
of the paternal grandmother's sister, and of the
father's maternal uncle; (उ), n. relationship by the
father's side.
—पितृ-बान्धव, अस्, m. a kins-
man in the paternal line.
—पितृ-भक्त, अस्, आ,
अम्, dutifully attached to a father.
—पितृ-भक्ति,
इस्, f. filial duty to a father.
—पितृभक्ति-तरङ्-
गिणी, f., N. of a work.
—पितृ-भूति, इस्, m., N. of a
commentator on Kātyāyana's Śrauta-sūtras.
—पितृ-
भोजन, अम्, n. a father's food; food offered to the
Manes; (अस्, अम्), m. n. the plant Phaseolus Radi-
atus (a species of pulse = माष).
—पितृ-भ्रातृ,
ता, m. a father's brother, paternal uncle.
—पितृ-
मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a father, having an illus-
trious father; accompanied by the Manes, connected
with the Manes (as Soma or Yama); mentioning
the Manes or deceased ancestors.
—पितृ-मन्दिर,
अम्, n. a father's house, paternal mansion; ‘dwelling-
[]
place of ancestors,’ a cemetery.
—पितृ-मातृ-हीन,
अस्, आ, अम्, destitute of father and mother, orphan.
—पितृ-मेध or पितृ-यज्ञ, अस्, m. sacrifice
offered to the Manes, obsequial offerings.
—पितृ-
याण, Ved. or पितृ-यान, अस्, आ, अम्, trodden by
the Manes; (अम्), n. the path trodden by the
Manes, the way leading to the Manes; the vehicle
of the Manes, a car to convey holy persons after their
decease to heaven.
—पितृ-राज्, ट्, or पितृ-राज, अस्,
or पितृ-राजन्, आ, m. ‘king of the Manes,’ an
epithet of Yama.
—पितृ-रूप, अस्, m., N. of a
Rudra.
—पितृ-लोक, अस्, m. a father's house, paternal
mansion; the world or sphere of the Manes (to
which various situations are ascribed, but principally
the Bhuvas region or mid-heaven).
—पितृ-वंश,
अस्, m. the paternal family.
—१. पितृ-वत्, आन्, अती,
अत्, having a father, whose father is living.
—२. पितृ-
वत्, ind. like a father; like the Manes; as if for the
Manes; as in the sacrifice offered to the Manes.
—पि-
तृ-वन, अम्, n. ‘grove of ancestors,’ a cemetery, a
place where dead bodies are burnt or buried.
—पि-
तृवने-चर, अस्, ई, अम्, haunting a cemetery; (अस्),
m. an epithet of Śiva; a goblin.
—पितृ-वर्तिन्, ई,
m. ‘staying or abiding with ancestors,’ N. of a
Brāhman (= king Brahma-datta).
—पितृ-वसति,
इस्, f. ‘abode of departed ancestors,’ a cemetery.
—पितृ-वाक्-पर, अस्, आ, अम्, attentive to the
voice of parents, obedient to parents.
—पितृ-
वित्त, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. acquired by ancestors; (Sāy.)
= पितुः सकाशाल् लब्ध, derived from a father,
patrimonial.
—पितृ-व्रत, अस्, m. a worshipper of
the Manes; (अम्), n. worship of ancestors, obsequial
rites.
—पितृ-शर्मन्, आ, m., N. of a Dānava.
—पितृ-श्रवण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. bringing honour
to a father; (Sāy. = पिता प्रख्यायते येन पु-
त्रेण तादृशः.)
—पितृ-श्राद्ध, अम्, n. a
funeral ceremony or obsequial rites in honour of
a father or deceased ancestor.
—पितृ-षद्, त्, त्,
त्, Ved. living unmarried with a father or with
parents; ‘dwelling with the Manes,’ an epithet of
Rudra.
—पितृ-षदन, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. inhabited
by the Manes.
—पितृ-ष्वसृ, सा, f. a father's
sister, paternal aunt (= पितुः-ष्वसृ).
—पितृ-
ष्वस्रीय, अस्, आ, m. f. a father's sister's son or
daughter, a paternal aunt's son or daughter.
—पितृ-
सन्निभ, अस्, आ, अम्, like a father, fatherly, paternal.
—पितृ-सामान्य, अम्, n. ancestors collectively.
—पितृ-सू, ऊस्, f. a father's mother; ‘mother of the
Manes,’ twilight; [cf. पितृ-प्रसू.]
—पितृ-सूक्त,
अम्, n., N. of a Vedic hymn.
—पितृ-स्थान, अस्,
m. a guardian; (अम्), n. the sphere of the Manes.
—पितृस्थानीय, अस्, m. a guardian (who takes the
place of a parent).
—पितृ-स्वसृ, सा, f. an incorrect
form for पितृ-ष्वसृ.
—पितृस्वस्रीय, अस्, आ, m.
f., see पितृष्वस्रीय.
—पितृ-हत्या, f. the murder
of a father, parricide.
—पितृ-हन्, आ, m. a parricide.
—पितृ-हू, ऊस्, ऊस्, उ, invoking or dedicated to the
Pitṛs; (ऊस्), f., scil. द्वार्, N. of the southern aper-
ture of the human body, i. e. of the right ear; [cf.
देव-हू.]
—पितृ-हूय, अम्, n., Ved. invoking or
summoning deceased ancestors.
—पित्रर्जित (˚तृ-
अर्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, derived from a father; property
originally acquired by a father.
—पित्रर्थम् (˚तृ-
अर्˚), ind. for a father's sake.

पितृक, अस्, आ, अम्, (at the end of a comp.)
paternal, parental, ancestral, relating or belonging to
parents or progenitors, obsequial.

पित्र्य, अस्, आ, अम्, derived from a father, relating
to a father, paternal, patrimonial, ancestral, belonging
to a father or to progenitors, usual or customary with
a father; relating to deceased ancestors, consecrated
to the Manes, referring or devoted to the Manes,
obsequial; in Manu II. 59. पित्र्यं तीर्थम् = the
part of the hand sacred to deified progenitors, i. e.
the part between the fore-finger and thumb; (अस्),
m. the eldest brother (who takes the place of a
father); the month Māgha; (आ), f. the Nakṣatra
Maghā (presided over by the Manes); the day of
[]
full moon, the worship of the Manes on the day
of full moon; (अम्), n., scil. कर्म, the worship
of the Manes; the Nakṣatra Maghā; the part of
the hand between the fore-finger and thumb.
—पित्र्या-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. (perhaps) possess-
ing property inherited from a father; (Sāy.) =
पितृ-मत्, q. v.

पित्त पित्त, अम्, n. (etymology doubtful),
bile, the bilious humor, one of the three humors of
the body (the other two being वात and कफ; it
is especially secreted between the stomach and
bowels, and thence flows through the liver, and
distributes itself in the spleen, heart, eyes, and skin;
its chief quality is heat); [cf. कूर्म-प्˚, गो-प्˚,
रक्त-प्˚, पैत्तिक.]
—पित्त-कोष, अस्, m. the
gall-bladder.
—पित्त-क्षोभ, अस्, m. excess and
disturbance of the bilious humor.
—पित्त-गदिन्, ई,
इनी, इ, suffering from bilious complaints, bilious.
—पित्त-घ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, ‘bile-destroying,’ anti-
bilious; (अम्), n. an antidote to bilious com-
plaints; ghee ?; (ई), f. a plant, Cocculus Cordifolius.
—पित्त-ज्वर, अस्, m. bilious fever.
—पित्त-द्रा-
विन्, ई, इणी, इ, ‘bile-dispersing,’ removing bile; (ई),
m. the sweet citron (= मधुर-जम्बीर).
—पित्त-
धर, अस्, आ, अम्, containing bile, bilious.
—पित्त-
निवर्हण, अस्, आ, अम्, destroying bile.
—पित्त-
प्रकृति, इस्, इस्, इ, being of a bilious temperament.
—पित्त-प्रकोप, अस्, m. excess and vitiation of
the bilious humor.
—पित्त-रक्त, अम्, n. plethora;
[cf. रक्त-पित्त.]
—पित्त-रोगिन्, ई, इणी, इ, suffering
from bilious complaints, bilious.
—पित्त-वत्, आन्,
अती, अत्, having bile, bilious.
—पित्त-वायु, उस्, m.
flatulence arising from excess and vitiation of the
bilious humor.
—पित्त-विदग्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, burnt
up by bile, impaired or destroyed by bile.
—पित्त-
विनाशन, अस्, ई, अम्, ‘bile-destroying,’ antibilious.
—पित्त-शमन, अस्, ई, अम्, ‘bile-alleviating,’
antibilious.
—पित्त-स्यन्द, अस्, m. a bilious form
of ophthalmia; [cf. पित्ताभिष्यन्द.]
—पित्त-
हर, अस्, ई, अम्, ‘bile-removing,’ antibilious.
—पित्-
तातीसार (˚त-अत्˚), अस्, m. ‘bile-dysentery,’ a bilious
form of diarrhœa.
—पित्तातीसारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, suffering
from a bilious form of dysentery.
—पित्ताभिष्यन्द
(˚त-अभ्˚), अस्, m. a bilious form of ophthalmia;
[cf. पित्त-स्यन्द.]
—पित्तारि (˚त-अरि), इस्, m.
‘enemy of bile,’ i. e. anything antibilious; N. of
various plants and vegetable substances used to coun-
teract biliousness (= पर्पट, लाक्षा, and वर्वर).
—पित्तोपहत (˚त-उप्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, impaired or
destroyed by bile.

पीत 1. पीत, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. 1. पा), drunk,
quaffed; drunk in, imbibed; soaked, steeped, satu-
rated, filled with; (अम्), n. drinking.
—पीत-तैल,
